laws.rule: Under Busan's ordinance on creating a smoke-free environment, the area within 10 metres of a taxi stand became a smoke-free zone on 1 September 2025, with a fine of KRW 50,000 (about A$53.13, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = KRW 941.07) starting in December 2025. A news report says bus stops and subway station entrances were already covered. The city's own page could not be read, so confirm with Busan Metropolitan City.

Busan Metropolitan City can designate outdoor places as smoke-free under the National Health Promotion Act. The ordinance lists the kinds of place it can cover: city parks, bus stops and taxi stands, beaches, riverside walking paths, busy streets and tourist or shopping areas, school routes, the area within 10 metres of urban rail exits, crossings (5 metres), traditional markets and public toilets. The exact designated sites are set by notice and marked by signs, so follow the signs. The fine is KRW 50,000 (about A$53.13, RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = KRW 941.07).

sources.title: Busan Expands Smoke-Free Zones to Taxi Stands, Fines Begin in December
